turns.text: quick q can you build me a weekly study schedule for my network cert. i work mon-fri 2pm to 10:30pm so it has to be mornings. also dont put anything late at night, im usually asleep by 1 and up around 9. i use a practice test app plus a secondhand study guide with tabbed chapters. port numbers are still shaky so weight those heavier pls

Happy to. With work 2 p.m. to 10:30 p.m. and you up around 9, mornings are your window. Here's a realistic week:

**Mon-Fri (before work)**
- 9:45-10:15: wake up, eat, get going
- 10:15-11:15: study block (60 min)
- 11:15 on: free time before heading to work

**Block focus**
- Mon: Port numbers. Make flashcards (port, protocol, TCP/UDP) and drill 20 minutes, then read one tabbed chapter in the guide
- Tue: Port numbers again, quiz yourself cold, then 20 practice-app questions
- Wed: Study guide chapter on a different topic, plus a short port review at the end
- Thu: Port numbers drill, then a timed set in the practice app
- Fri: Review everything you missed in the app this week, plus 10 minutes of ports

**Weekends**
- Sat: One full practice test in the app, then go through wrong answers
- Sun: Light day. 30 minutes on the weakest topic from Saturday's test

Ports get about 25-30 minutes of most sessions, which is the heaviest weighting in the plan. Nothing is scheduled after 11 p.m. so your sleep stays protected.

Tip for ports: group them by purpose (web, email, remote access, file transfer) instead of memorizing a flat list. Want a grouped cheat sheet to start your Monday flashcards?

**Ports cheat sheet**

**Web**
- 80 HTTP
- 443 HTTPS

**Email**
- 25 SMTP
- 110 POP3
- 143 IMAP

**Remote access**
- 22 SSH
- 23 Telnet
- 3389 RDP

**File transfer**
- 20/21 FTP
- 69 TFTP

**Network services**
- 53 DNS
- 67/68 DHCP
- 123 NTP
- 161/162 SNMP

Drill: cover the name, say the number, then flip it. Missed ones go in a separate pile for the next session.
Glad it helps! Good luck with the drills. If you want, I can make a quiz of 20 mixed port questions with the answers hidden until you ask.
